pathway.title: Victory Capital Holdings, Inc. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: 1. The standalone balance sheet carries one debt instrument, the term loan under the 2019 Credit Agreement of USD 975.15 million at September 30, 2026, alongside an undrawn USD 100.0 million revolver, described as first lien, maturing September 23, 2030 [CP-1 capital structure]. The interest rate is 5.82%, floating at SOFR plus 1.75% since the May 18, 2026 repricing. Leverage on management's adjusted EBITDA fell from 1.44x at FY2025 to 1.14x at the last twelve months to Q3 2026 [CP-1 leverage chart]; the fall comes from higher EBITDA (USD 682.851 million to USD 856.348 million) and from the FY2025 figure including only three quarters of the Amundi US business, which means the comparison flatters the improvement. On the stricter proxy of operating income plus depreciation and amortization (USD 727.102 million), leverage is 1.34x gross and 1.06x net [CP-1 definition risks]. Either way leverage is far under the single covenant level of 4.00x, but that covenant is defined on first lien debt and a covenant EBITDA that are not in the sources, so headroom is Not calculable.

2. Cash interest cover rose from 8.57x at FY2025 to 14.83x on the last twelve months [CP-1 interest cover chart], and part of that rise is the last-twelve-months window dropping an unexplained third quarter of 2025 cash interest payment of USD 30.025 million. Third quarter of 2026 cash interest was USD 13.696 million, so the last-twelve-months cash interest of USD 57.742 million is not out of line with the recent quarterly pace.

3. Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was USD 307.724 million against USD 170.126 million at June 30, 2026. The change is cash: USD 207.724 million against USD 70.126 million, with the revolver unchanged [CP-1 liquidity]. Calls on it include USD 53.8 million of contingent consideration for the WestEnd acquisition estimated payable within a year, quarterly term loan amortization of about USD 2.46 million, the dividend of USD 0.50 a share payable December 23, 2026, and the unknown cash portion of First Eagle. Part of consolidated cash sits in a regulated broker-dealer whose cash is generally not available for corporate purposes [CP-1 claims outside debt]; the split is Not supplied.

4. Cash generation is strong but is allocated to equity holders. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD 621.193 million over the last twelve months [CP-1 calculations], 0.64x of gross debt (calculated below). In nine months 2026 dividends, repurchases, taxes on net share settlement and contingent payments used USD 443.212 million of USD 479.74 million operating cash flow, 92.4% (calculated below), and net term loan repayment was USD 7.388 million [CP-1 cash flow]. This is Analyst Interpretation: nothing in the sources shows these distributions funded by debt, and no creditor-adverse action is documented [CP-1A governance], but the credit agreement's restricted payment terms are not supplied, so legal capacity to distribute is unknown.

5. The business model concentrates risk in assets and people rather than in assets on the balance sheet. Revenue is fees on assets; fund advisory contracts are terminable on not more than 60 days' notice; the largest franchise, Pioneer Investments, was acquired from Amundi and sits at about the 42% ceiling the company states; Amundi is also a 26.1% fully diluted holder with two board nomination rights and the exclusive offshore distributor [CP-1A operating model; ownership]. Management says about two-thirds of operating expense is variable, a Management Language claim, but personnel compensation rose in the third quarter of 2026, so the cushion is not proved [CP-1A operating model].

6. First Eagle changes the credit profile. Consideration is cash, new common stock and a new series of non-voting convertible preferred stock, funded in part under a debt commitment letter; closing is expected by the end of the first quarter of 2027, subject to stockholder, regulatory and client approvals; stockholder litigation seeks to delay it [CP-1A transaction summary]. No amounts are given. Any post-closing leverage, liquidity, ranking or covenant statement is Not calculable and is withheld.

runs.text: Strengths. (1) Low standalone leverage and strong cover on the sources' own measures, Documentary Fact from the CP-1 tables, with the caveat that adjusted EBITDA is a management measure that adds back share-based compensation and acquisition costs; the stricter proxy still gives a leverage level well within the covenant level. (2) A long, simple debt structure: one term loan to September 23, 2032, amortizing 1% a year, with calculated annual maturities of USD 9.85 million before the bullet of about USD 918.5 million, and a revolver to September 23, 2030 that is undrawn (Documentary Fact for the dates, Analyst Interpretation for the calculated schedule). (3) Liquidity of USD 307.724 million, with minimal capital spending of USD 3.024 million in nine months 2026 (Documentary Fact). (4) Scale and diversity across eight investment franchises, a Solutions Platform and four client channels, with the largest franchise at about 42% of assets under management (Documentary Fact). (5) Net inflows in the second and third quarters of 2026 after outflows in the first quarter of 2026 and in the nine months of 2025: USD 11.702 billion of long-term net inflows in the third quarter of 2026 (Management Language for "record", Documentary Fact for the amount).

Weaknesses. (1) Revenue visibility is short because fund advisory contracts can be ended on 60 days' notice and revenue moves with markets, flows and fee realization, which fell to 44.8 bp in the third quarter of 2026 from 47.9 bp in the second quarter (Documentary Fact). (2) Reliance on Amundi for ownership, board seats and offshore distribution concentrates a single counterparty (Documentary Fact); the Amundi preferred stock terms are Not supplied. (3) The pending First Eagle acquisition with undisclosed debt and a cash component creates leverage, execution and litigation risk (Documentary Fact for existence; the credit effect is Insufficient Information). (4) Earnings quality: adjusted EBITDA exceeds the proxy by USD 129.246 million (15.1% of adjusted EBITDA, calculated below), and the share-based compensation addback jumped in the third quarter of 2026 without the one-time part being separated (Documentary Fact). (5) Distributions to equity absorb most operating cash flow, leaving debt reduction at the scheduled amount (Analyst Interpretation). (6) Absent monitoring data: covenant ratio, guarantors and collateral, restricted payment capacity and ratings (Insufficient Information).

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The Amundi US transaction closed on April 1, 2025. In exchange for all the shares of Amundi's U.S. business, Victory issued 3,293,471 shares of common stock and 19,698,274 shares of preferred stock (net of 44,026 preferred shares forfeited in a post-closing adjustment on August 1, 2025, per 10-K page:109), together 26.1% of fully diluted shares; the purchase price was approximately 1,326 US$ million, settled entirely in Company shares (Q3-10Q page:11). The 10-K exhibit index lists a certificate of designations for Series A Non-Voting Convertible Preferred Stock, and Amundi may require Victory to nominate two Amundi designees to the board (10-K page:135). Alongside the equity, Victory and Amundi entered exclusive distribution agreements, a 15-year exclusive offshore distribution arrangement that auto-renews in 2040 (10-K page:14). The purchase price allocation was finalized in Q1 2026 (Q3-10Q page:12). Pioneer Investments contributed revenue of about 155 US$ million in Q3 2026 and 517 US$ million in nine months 2026, and the filing states that net income attributable to Pioneer is "impractical to determine" because discrete franchise-level financial information is not prepared (Q3-10Q page:12). The Amundi deal is a completed transaction, so for creditors it explains the 2025 jump in assets and in goodwill and intangibles, not a new financing event.

Debt events in the period are refinancings, not new money. On September 23, 2025 the Sixth Amendment extended the revolver to September 23, 2030 and repriced the term loan at 985.0 US$ million; on May 18, 2026 the Seventh Amendment repriced the term loan to SOFR plus 1.75% (Q2-10Q page:18; Q3-10Q page:20). No bond, note or other new debt issue appears in the pack. Costs of the Seventh Amendment were 2.4 US$ million, of which 2.0 US$ million was a loss on debt extinguishment (Q3-10Q page:21).

The pending First Eagle transaction, all of it a subsequent event relative to the Q2 2026 reports and still pending at the cutoff, is described in the Q3 2026 report: on August 25, 2026 Victory agreed to acquire GC Ferry Holdings, Inc. from GC Ferry Parent, L.P. through a two-step merger; consideration is a combination of cash, newly issued common stock and a new series of non-voting convertible preferred stock; Victory entered a debt commitment letter with certain financial institutions to fund the cash portion and related fees; closing is expected by the end of the first quarter of 2027, subject to approval by Victory stockholders, regulatory approvals and client consents (Q3-10Q pages:12 and 13). Management calls it "transformational" and says it adds a scaled CLO and alternative credit platform (R3 page:2), which is Management Language. For a creditor the mechanics are: cash consideration funded by new debt raises leverage from the current low standalone level by an amount that is not disclosed; new preferred stock adds a senior-to-common claim, as the Amundi preferred already is; share issuance dilutes and may shift control, and the closing depends on stockholder and client consents, so completion risk and the post-closing capital structure are both open. Transaction costs already expensed were 15.5 US$ million in Q3 2026 and 22.5 US$ million in nine months 2026 (Q3-10Q page:13). Litigation followed the proxy: two stockholder complaints and ten demand letters seek, among other things, to enjoin closing until more disclosure is made (Q3-10Q page:48); Victory calls them without merit and gives no loss estimate. No amount of consideration, cash portion, commitment size, lenders, pricing, ticking fees or conditions of the financing is in the pack, and no First Eagle financial statements are supplied, so the new debt issue, pro forma leverage, and pro forma liquidity are Not supplied and Not calculable. Dated after the Q3 reporting period but inside the cutoff: the definitive proxy statement (October 16, 2026) and the dividend of 0.50 dollars per share approved on November 4, 2026.

fields.value: The 2019 Credit Agreement carries one financial maintenance covenant: a first lien leverage ratio of no greater than 4.00 to 1.00, tested at the end of each fiscal quarter only when revolver borrowings exceed 35.0% of commitments (Q3-10Q page:20). With a 100.0 million dollar commitment the test is not triggered unless more than 35.0 million dollars is drawn (calculated), and the revolver is undrawn. There is no step-down printed. The company states it was in compliance at September 30, 2026. The reported covenant ratio, the covenant definition of EBITDA and first lien debt, and any add-back cap are Not supplied, so headroom is Not calculable. For orientation only, gross term loan principal over the calculated LTM adjusted EBITDA is 1.14x; this is not the covenant metric, because the covenant is defined on first lien debt and a covenant EBITDA that is not in the pack.

fields.value: Adjusted EBITDA (US$ thousands) is the company's measure: 856,348 on an LTM basis against 727,102 for the stricter proxy of income from operations plus depreciation and amortization, a calculated difference of 129,246 that rests on the reconciliation's addbacks and is not decomposed here. The addbacks include share-based compensation, which the footnote describes as "associated with equity awards in connection with acquisitions and certain one-time performance-based shares" (Q3-10Q page:43), acquisition, restructuring and exit costs, other business taxes, and debt issuance costs. The share-based compensation addback is 32,547 in Q3 2026 against 2,022 in Q3 2025 (Q3-10Q page:42), and the filings do not separate the one-time part. On the proxy, leverage at September 30, 2026 is 1.34x gross and 1.06x net, against 1.14x and 0.90x on adjusted EBITDA. Both are far below the 4.00x covenant level, but that level is a different metric. Pro forma Amundi US data is given only for revenue and net income, not EBITDA (Q3-10Q page:12), so no pro forma EBITDA exists in the pack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Victory Capital is a diversified, asset-based investment manager whose credit profile rests on three things the sources document. First, a fee-on-assets revenue model: revenue moves with average assets under management, the fee rate and net flows, and fund advisory agreements are cancellable on short notice, so revenue is recurring in form but not contractually locked. Second, a multi-franchise, centralized-platform structure that management says keeps about two-thirds of operating expense variable and capital spending minimal, which supports cash conversion but depends on the investment teams being retained. Third, a strategic relationship with Amundi that is at once shareholder, board-nominating party, exclusive offshore distributor and exclusive supplier of Amundi's active products into the United States, which concentrates ownership, distribution and governance in one counterparty. The consolidated company's only debt is one term loan with an undrawn revolver (CP-1); ownership has no sponsor named, but no controlling-holder register is in the pack beyond Amundi and employee ownership. The transaction that matters most to a creditor is the pending acquisition of First Eagle for cash, common shares and a new series of non-voting convertible preferred stock, financed in part by a debt commitment letter whose amount and terms are not in the pack. All views here are on the standalone, pre-First Eagle company, and every First Eagle consequence is a gap, not a conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Amundi US transaction closed on April 1, 2025. In exchange for all the shares of Amundi's U.S. business, Victory issued 3,293,471 shares of common stock and 19,698,274 shares of preferred stock (net of 44,026 preferred shares forfeited in a post-closing adjustment on August 1, 2025, per 10-K page:109), together 26.1% of fully diluted shares; the purchase price was approximately 1,326 US$ million, settled entirely in Company shares (Q3-10Q page:11). The 10-K exhibit index lists a certificate of designations for Series A Non-Voting Convertible Preferred Stock, and Amundi may require Victory to nominate two Amundi designees to the board (10-K page:135). Alongside the equity, Victory and Amundi entered exclusive distribution agreements, a 15-year exclusive offshore distribution arrangement that auto-renews in 2040 (10-K page:14). The purchase price allocation was finalized in Q1 2026 (Q3-10Q page:12). Pioneer Investments contributed revenue of about 155 US$ million in Q3 2026 and 517 US$ million in nine months 2026, and the filing states that net income attributable to Pioneer is "impractical to determine" because discrete franchise-level financial information is not prepared (Q3-10Q page:12). The Amundi deal is a completed transaction, so for creditors it explains the 2025 jump in assets and in goodwill and intangibles, not a new financing event.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt events in the period are refinancings, not new money. On September 23, 2025 the Sixth Amendment extended the revolver to September 23, 2030 and repriced the term loan at 985.0 US$ million; on May 18, 2026 the Seventh Amendment repriced the term loan to SOFR plus 1.75% (Q2-10Q page:18; Q3-10Q page:20). No bond, note or other new debt issue appears in the pack. Costs of the Seventh Amendment were 2.4 US$ million, of which 2.0 US$ million was a loss on debt extinguishment (Q3-10Q page:21).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The pending First Eagle transaction, all of it a subsequent event relative to the Q2 2026 reports and still pending at the cutoff, is described in the Q3 2026 report: on August 25, 2026 Victory agreed to acquire GC Ferry Holdings, Inc. from GC Ferry Parent, L.P. through a two-step merger; consideration is a combination of cash, newly issued common stock and a new series of non-voting convertible preferred stock; Victory entered a debt commitment letter with certain financial institutions to fund the cash portion and related fees; closing is expected by the end of the first quarter of 2027, subject to approval by Victory stockholders, regulatory approvals and client consents (Q3-10Q pages:12 and 13). Management calls it "transformational" and says it adds a scaled CLO and alternative credit platform (R3 page:2), which is Management Language. For a creditor the mechanics are: cash consideration funded by new debt raises leverage from the current low standalone level by an amount that is not disclosed; new preferred stock adds a senior-to-common claim, as the Amundi preferred already is; share issuance dilutes and may shift control, and the closing depends on stockholder and client consents, so completion risk and the post-closing capital structure are both open. Transaction costs already expensed were 15.5 US$ million in Q3 2026 and 22.5 US$ million in nine months 2026 (Q3-10Q page:13). Litigation followed the proxy: two stockholder complaints and ten demand letters seek, among other things, to enjoin closing until more disclosure is made (Q3-10Q page:48); Victory calls them without merit and gives no loss estimate. No amount of consideration, cash portion, commitment size, lenders, pricing, ticking fees or conditions of the financing is in the pack, and no First Eagle financial statements are supplied, so the new debt issue, pro forma leverage, and pro forma liquidity are Not supplied and Not calculable. Dated after the Q3 reporting period but inside the cutoff: the definitive proxy statement (October 16, 2026) and the dividend of 0.50 dollars per share approved on November 4, 2026.

fields.value: Victory Capital's standalone credit profile is sound on every measure the sources allow, but the credit view after the First Eagle acquisition is open. The strongest support is balance sheet and cash generation: USD 975.15 million of term loan against USD 856.348 million of last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA (1.14x gross, 0.90x net), cash interest cover of 14.83x, USD 307.724 million of liquidity and a first maturity of any size in September 2032. The weakest point is that earnings are fee income on assets that clients can withdraw on short notice, and a large cash-and-shares acquisition is pending whose debt, terms and target financials are not in the sources. What decides the outcome is the size and pricing of the First Eagle financing, whether closing happens as planned, and whether net inflows persist after the record third quarter of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. The standalone balance sheet carries one debt instrument, the term loan under the 2019 Credit Agreement of USD 975.15 million at September 30, 2026, alongside an undrawn USD 100.0 million revolver, described as first lien, maturing September 23, 2030 [CP-1 capital structure]. The interest rate is 5.82%, floating at SOFR plus 1.75% since the May 18, 2026 repricing. Leverage on management's adjusted EBITDA fell from 1.44x at FY2025 to 1.14x at the last twelve months to Q3 2026 [CP-1 leverage chart]; the fall comes from higher EBITDA (USD 682.851 million to USD 856.348 million) and from the FY2025 figure including only three quarters of the Amundi US business, which means the comparison flatters the improvement. On the stricter proxy of operating income plus depreciation and amortization (USD 727.102 million), leverage is 1.34x gross and 1.06x net [CP-1 definition risks]. Either way leverage is far under the single covenant level of 4.00x, but that covenant is defined on first lien debt and a covenant EBITDA that are not in the sources, so headroom is Not calculable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Cash interest cover rose from 8.57x at FY2025 to 14.83x on the last twelve months [CP-1 interest cover chart], and part of that rise is the last-twelve-months window dropping an unexplained third quarter of 2025 cash interest payment of USD 30.025 million. Third quarter of 2026 cash interest was USD 13.696 million, so the last-twelve-months cash interest of USD 57.742 million is not out of line with the recent quarterly pace.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was USD 307.724 million against USD 170.126 million at June 30, 2026. The change is cash: USD 207.724 million against USD 70.126 million, with the revolver unchanged [CP-1 liquidity]. Calls on it include USD 53.8 million of contingent consideration for the WestEnd acquisition estimated payable within a year, quarterly term loan amortization of about USD 2.46 million, the dividend of USD 0.50 a share payable December 23, 2026, and the unknown cash portion of First Eagle. Part of consolidated cash sits in a regulated broker-dealer whose cash is generally not available for corporate purposes [CP-1 claims outside debt]; the split is Not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Cash generation is strong but is allocated to equity holders. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD 621.193 million over the last twelve months [CP-1 calculations], 0.64x of gross debt (calculated below). In nine months 2026 dividends, repurchases, taxes on net share settlement and contingent payments used USD 443.212 million of USD 479.74 million operating cash flow, 92.4% (calculated below), and net term loan repayment was USD 7.388 million [CP-1 cash flow]. This is Analyst Interpretation: nothing in the sources shows these distributions funded by debt, and no creditor-adverse action is documented [CP-1A governance], but the credit agreement's restricted payment terms are not supplied, so legal capacity to distribute is unknown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. The business model concentrates risk in assets and people rather than in assets on the balance sheet. Revenue is fees on assets; fund advisory contracts are terminable on not more than 60 days' notice; the largest franchise, Pioneer Investments, was acquired from Amundi and sits at about the 42% ceiling the company states; Amundi is also a 26.1% fully diluted holder with two board nomination rights and the exclusive offshore distributor [CP-1A operating model; ownership]. Management says about two-thirds of operating expense is variable, a Management Language claim, but personnel compensation rose in the third quarter of 2026, so the cushion is not proved [CP-1A operating model].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. First Eagle changes the credit profile. Consideration is cash, new common stock and a new series of non-voting convertible preferred stock, funded in part under a debt commitment letter; closing is expected by the end of the first quarter of 2027, subject to stockholder, regulatory and client approvals; stockholder litigation seeks to delay it [CP-1A transaction summary]. No amounts are given. Any post-closing leverage, liquidity, ranking or covenant statement is Not calculable and is withheld.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. (1) Low standalone leverage and strong cover on the sources' own measures, Documentary Fact from the CP-1 tables, with the caveat that adjusted EBITDA is a management measure that adds back share-based compensation and acquisition costs; the stricter proxy still gives a leverage level well within the covenant level. (2) A long, simple debt structure: one term loan to September 23, 2032, amortizing 1% a year, with calculated annual maturities of USD 9.85 million before the bullet of about USD 918.5 million, and a revolver to September 23, 2030 that is undrawn (Documentary Fact for the dates, Analyst Interpretation for the calculated schedule). (3) Liquidity of USD 307.724 million, with minimal capital spending of USD 3.024 million in nine months 2026 (Documentary Fact). (4) Scale and diversity across eight investment franchises, a Solutions Platform and four client channels, with the largest franchise at about 42% of assets under management (Documentary Fact). (5) Net inflows in the second and third quarters of 2026 after outflows in the first quarter of 2026 and in the nine months of 2025: USD 11.702 billion of long-term net inflows in the third quarter of 2026 (Management Language for "record", Documentary Fact for the amount).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. (1) Revenue visibility is short because fund advisory contracts can be ended on 60 days' notice and revenue moves with markets, flows and fee realization, which fell to 44.8 bp in the third quarter of 2026 from 47.9 bp in the second quarter (Documentary Fact). (2) Reliance on Amundi for ownership, board seats and offshore distribution concentrates a single counterparty (Documentary Fact); the Amundi preferred stock terms are Not supplied. (3) The pending First Eagle acquisition with undisclosed debt and a cash component creates leverage, execution and litigation risk (Documentary Fact for existence; the credit effect is Insufficient Information). (4) Earnings quality: adjusted EBITDA exceeds the proxy by USD 129.246 million (15.1% of adjusted EBITDA, calculated below), and the share-based compensation addback jumped in the third quarter of 2026 without the one-time part being separated (Documentary Fact). (5) Distributions to equity absorb most operating cash flow, leaving debt reduction at the scheduled amount (Analyst Interpretation). (6) Absent monitoring data: covenant ratio, guarantors and collateral, restricted payment capacity and ratings (Insufficient Information).
